name: GRACE LING
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $1142 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Sculptural womenswear, knit dresses and tailoring with 3D-printed metal bags and jewelry, roughly $400–$2,400, sold from its New York store and website.

quote.q: GRACE LING is about a sense of eccentric elegance and intelligent femininity. It is a fashion label founded on 3D-printing and CGI technology.

price_read.sublines: Grace Ling women's ready-to-wear (much of it pre-order by season); EXCLUDED: bags, jewellery, accessories, bralettes

doors.note: One NYC flagship store in an upper-floor suite (Garment District), Mon-Fri 11-6, walk-ins welcome, appointments encouraged — borderline studio/showroom but brand calls it flagship store selling full online assortment.

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 80 of 127 styles (244 feed records less 20 bags, 9 jewelry, 3 accessories and a home object = 211 listings, collapsed on the title before '

craft_evidence.owned: claim only — 'a fashion label founded on 3D-printing and CGI technology'; no workshop named or shown; one NYC store
craft_evidence.mills: no — 'Italian viscose', 'Italian lux viscose' and 'Italian calf' are origin words, no mill
craft_evidence.madein: ~4% (3 of 80 sampled styles state 'MADE IN NEW YORK'; 51 'made/crafted in' hits across the feed are mostly cloth descrip
craft_evidence.heritage: vague — no founding date or place on the about page
craft_evidence.process: partial — 3D-printed metal trims and CGI pattern work for zero-waste cutting are described, not shown
craft_evidence.reasoning: A few pages state 'Made in New York', and the about page describes a 3D-printing and CGI method for the metal hardware and patterns. No workshop, maker or mill is named and nothing is dated. A place on a few pages plus an undocumented method is a 2.
